{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement  
**Status:** 19 findings reviewed — 17 compliant, 2 deviations (1 critical, 1 high)

---

## 1. Executive summary

The draft is, on the whole, unusually favourable to us and materially aligned with our playbook. The critical protections are already in place: Vendor IP and conduct indemnities covering us and our Affiliates and sitting outside the cap as Excluded Claims (§ 20, § 21.3); our ownership of Customer Data and Deliverables with no reach-through to our pre-existing IP (§ 14); a broad, perpetual, transferable licence grant extending to Affiliates and contractors (§ 13); assignment and change-of-control controls that bind Vendor but not us (§ 24); and a convenience termination right with pro-rata refund and no early-termination fee (§ 9.4 / § 29.4). We are also free of the customer-side restrictions we most often have to negotiate out — no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum commitments, no non-solicit and no MFN burdening us (§ 2.1, § 7.1, § 12.3, § 12.4).

Two items require redlines before signature.

First, and most importantly, the liability cap in § 21 is illusory. The architecture is correct — mutual cap, mutual exclusion of indirect damages, a well-drawn Excluded Claims carve-out, and payment obligations excluded from "damages" — but "Fees" is defined in § 1.5/1.6 as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form. The practical effect is a USD 12,000 cap rather than a 12-months'-fees cap. We have redlined the cap basis to the greater of all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement in the preceding 12 months and USD 1,000,000.

Second, § 7.7 imposes liquidated damages on us at 15% of annual Fees per week of delay. That is punitive, potentially unlimited in aggregate, and cuts across our right to withhold disputed amounts under § 7.3. Our position is no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer; we have deleted the clause and offered simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts as the fallback.

Everything else can be accepted as drafted.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 21 LIMITATION OF LIABILITY | Cap quantum illusory: "Fees" defined in § 1.5/1.6 as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee. Redlined to greater of trailing 12 months' amounts paid or payable and USD 1,000,000. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES | § 7.7 imposes 15% of annual Fees per week of delay on us; punitive and inconsistent with § 7.3 withholding right. Deleted; interest on undisputed overdue amounts offered as fallback. |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 INDEMNIFICATION | IP indemnity covers us and Affiliates (20.1); further indemnities for breach of law, bodily injury/property damage, Customer Data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud (20.2); our indemnity narrow (20.3); remedies additional to defence (20.5); Excluded Claims under 21.3. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND DELIVERABLES | We own Customer Data and pre-existing IP (14.1) and Deliverables by assignment (14.2); Vendor retains only Vendor Technology with licence back under 13.2 (14.3); no joint ownership or feedback assignment (14.4). |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 ASSIGNMENT AND CHANGE OF CONTROL | Affiliate/M&A assignment without consent (24.1); Vendor restricted and barred from competitor transfers (24.2); no Vendor right triggered by our change of control (24.4). |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 AGREEMENT STRUCTURE AND SCOPE | No sole-supplier obligation; 2.1 confirms we pay only for Services ordered and declining to order is not a breach; 12.3 preserves supplier choice. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 ACCESS RIGHTS AND LICENCE | Grant covers Affiliates and contractors (13.1); paid-up licences perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free with modification/derivative rights (13.2); transferable and revocable only for uncured material breach (13.3). |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12 CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITIES | 12.3 preserves our freedom to develop, acquire or sell any product in any field or territory; the only competitive covenant (12.4) binds Vendor. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 TERMINATION | Convenience right on 30 days' notice (9.4 with 29.4), pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, no early-termination fee; Vendor has no convenience right. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 AUDIT RIGHTS | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable via independent auditor; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%; no direct system access (22.2). |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION | New York law, exclusive jurisdiction in New York County; no mandatory arbitration, escalation does not delay urgent relief. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7 FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES | Only MFN runs in our favour (7.6); 12.3 confirms no most-favoured-customer commitment from us. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2 AGREEMENT STRUCTURE AND SCOPE | 2.1 disclaims purchase commitment; 7.1 bars unstated minimum-use charges; 12.3 confirms no minimum-volume commitment. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITIES | No non-solicit or no-hire binds us; 12.3 expressly confirms this and preserves general-recruitment hiring. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 8 TERM AND RENEWAL | 12-month renewals with 30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder (deadline extended if missed), uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3% on 90 days' notice. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND DATA RETURN | Six months' assistance at Order Form rates; data returned within 30 days in machine-readable format with metadata, no fee-dispute holdback; certified deletion only after we confirm return (11.3). |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19 WARRANTIES | Workmanlike warranty, 90-day Deliverable conformance, term-long hosted Services conformance, termination-and-refund backstop (19.4), compliance-with-law and no-malicious-code warranties (19.3); disclaimer in 19.5 does not limit express warranties. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 INSURANCE | CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, workers' comp; term plus one year; certificates on request and notice of cancellation; insurance does not cap Vendor liability. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **Liability cap quantum (§ 21, read with § 1.5/1.6).** A cap that resolves to USD 12,000 is not a commercially viable allocation of risk on this deal. We need the cap basis fixed to all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement in the preceding 12 months, floored at USD 1,000,000. The existing Excluded Claims construct in § 21.3 stays as drafted. This is the one point on which we should not sign without resolution.
2. **Customer-side liquidated damages (§ 7.7).** Our playbook position is no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer. Deletion is required. We can offer simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts as a fallback, but we should not accept a per-week percentage penalty, particularly while § 7.3 gives us a withholding right for disputed amounts.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. Issue the redline with the two changes above and the short `[Playbook]` comments explaining the cap-definition problem and the liquidated damages deletion.
2. Flag to the business owner that the § 21 cap issue is definitional rather than a negotiation over quantum — Vendor may well accept once the § 1.5/1.6 drafting artefact is explained.
3. Confirm with the deal owner that the USD 1,000,000 floor is proportionate to the expected contract value, and adjust before the redline goes out if the run-rate materially exceeds it.
4. Accept the remaining 17 positions as drafted; no further redlines required from us on those sections.
5. On return of Vendor's markup, re-check only § 7.7 and § 21 (plus any consequential changes to the § 1.5/1.6 definitions) before clearing for signature."}
